Levels marking
Level 1(1–3 marks)
Statements including limited detail which describe the benefits and/or
problems caused for a country by large amounts of immigration
Level 2(4–6 marks)
Uses named example.
More developed statements which describe the benefits and/or problems
caused for a country by large amounts of immigration
(Note: Max 5 if no named or inappropriate example.)
Level 3(7 marks)
Uses named example.
Comprehensive and accurate answer which describes the benefits and
problems caused for a country by large amounts of immigration, including
some place specific reference.
Content Guide:
Benefits:
Provide workers/skills
Will accept low pay/dirty jobs
Will pay taxes
Multi-cultural society/more diverse culture
Set up services (or example – food outlet, restaurant) etc.
Provides a larger market/demand for local production/sales/services or
example such as schools
More economic development/GNP/national income/contribute to
economy/country gets more money
Etc.
Problems:
Pressure on/need to provide more food supplies
Cost of/need for providing temporary accommodation/new housing/problems
caused by street dwellers/squatter settlements develop
High unemployment levels/financial support for unemployed
Conflicts with/resentment of local population
Cost/time/difficulty of processing immigrants
Need for patrols/rescue boats
Specified crime
Pressure on healthcare/education etc.
Note: answers must relate to problems for the country rather than for the
migrants to avoid overlap with (b)(ii)
Place specific reference is likely to consist of:
Named parts/settlements of the chosen country,
Population data
Migration data etc.

Levels marking
Level 1(1–3 marks)
Statements including limited detail which explain the reasons for the growth
and/or functions of a settlement
Level 2(4–6 marks)
Uses named example.
More developed statements which explain the reasons for the growth and/or
functions of a settlement
(Note: Max 5 if no named or inappropriate example.)
Level 3(7 marks)
Uses named example.
Comprehensive and accurate statements which explain the reasons for the
growth and functions of a settlement with some place specific reference.
Content Guide:
Answers will depend on the functions of the chosen settlement which may
include:
Port
Capital city
Industrial town
Route centre
Market town
Administrative centre
Tourist resort
Etc.
Reasons referred to may include:
Accessibility
Raw material/power availability
Scenic attractions
Surrounding land uses/land availability
Etc.
Place specific reference is likely to consist of:
Locational details
Specific details of land uses related to the function
Named parts of settlement etc.

Levels marking
Level 1(1–3 marks)
Statements including limited detail which describe the impacts of tropical
storms.
Level 2(4–6 marks)
Uses named example.
More developed statements which describe the impacts of tropical storms.
(Note: Max 5 if no named places included.)
Country = Max 5 unless small
Caribbean is ok.
Level 3(7 marks)
Comprehensive and accurate statements describe the impacts of tropical
storms including reference to named places.
Content Guide:
Answers are likely to refer to:
Death/injury
Damage to settlements/property/houses/roof slates blown off/chimneys
collapse/homelessness
Carpets ruined/possessions destroyed
Need to evacuate
Flooding
Roads damaged/flooded/access prevented/cars damaged
Water borne disease/cholera
Workplaces damaged/closed/people unable to work/fishing industry/port
activity disrupted
Schools/shops/churches (or another specific example) damaged
Electricity cut off
Water supplies polluted
Damage to boats
Cost of rebuilding
Dependence on welfare/aid
Crops/livestock/farmland destroyed/salination of soils/soil washed away
Fires caused (by lightning)
Etc.
Place specific reference is likely to consist of:
Locational details,
Specific details of the flood/impacts
Statistics/date etc.

Levels marking
Level 1(1–3 marks)
Statements including limited detail which describe the causes of an
earthquake.
Level 2(4–6 marks)
Uses named example
Developed statements which describe the causes of an earthquake.
(Note: Max 5 if no named or inappropriate example.)
E.g. Haiti/Nepal (Iceland/Indonesia/Japan not acceptable)
Level 3(7 marks)
Comprehensive and accurate statements which describe the causes of an
earthquake, including some place specific reference.
Content Guide:
Causes:
Location on plate boundary
Plate movement
Pressure build up
Friction
Pressure release
Seismic waves travel through crust
Etc.
Place specific reference is likely to consist of:
Locational details
Specific details of earthquake/date/time/depth
Names of plates
Statistical information.

Levels marking
Level 1(1–3 marks)
Statements including limited detail which describe the attractions of the
physical and/or human landscape of an area where tourism is important.
Level 2(4–6 marks)
Uses named example.
More developed statements which describe the attractions of the physical
and/or human landscape of an area where tourism is important.
(Note: Max 5 if no named or inappropriate example.) Country – ok if small
e.g. St Lucia/Barbados.
Level 3(7 marks)
Uses named example.
Comprehensive and accurate statements which describe the attractions of the
physical and human landscape of an area where tourism is important
including some place specific reference.
Content Guide:
Physical landscape:
Mountains
Lakes
Rivers/waterfalls
Beaches
Cliffs
Coral reefs
Tropical vegetation
Etc.
Human landscape:
Historical buildings
Restaurants
Theme parks
Hotel
Museums
Piers
Harbours/marinas
Etc.
Note: Accept appropriate activities as development of the physical or human
landscape e.g. mountains with hiking trails.
Place specific reference is likely to consist of:
Locational details;
Names of places/buildings within chosen area
Specific details.
